notes: Registered maintenance obligations of this repository, read by Devostasis when debt.source = file. An item belongs here when the current code carries a cost, not when a feature is missing: planned work lives in targets.json and ROADMAP.md. 'opened' is the date the obligation started being carried, 'updated' the last time it changed; an open item untouched for 30 days is stale.

items.title: Native change hotspots and local roots rely on recorded acquisition rather than complete ancestry proofs
items.cost: Implemented in the pending 0.6 assurance increment: code-analysis v2 authenticates bounded commit/parent/tree/blob proofs and independently derives roots, selection, completeness and edit counts offline. Rehashed claims are rejected; caps/shallow/missing objects remain explicit PARTIAL. V1 exact bytes/replay retain their documented acquisition-only limit. Independent PR review and maintainer release remain pending; issue #73.

items.title: Live candidate content recheck needs an explicit mutable source-ref binding
items.cost: Closed in the pending 0.4/0.5 implementation by named branch/PR/MR bindings with immutable source-project ids, commit membership and before/after handoff live resolution (issue #60). Historic v1 offline replay is preserved; legacy scopes need a freshly bound generation for automatic source handoff. Deployment and upstream release remain separate gates.

items.title: Large-project full GitLab collection still has incomplete bridge responses
items.cost: Bounded shared-budget concurrency and one per-generation train inventory improve throughput. Bridge/native response qualification and complete repeated generations remain issue #62; selected inventory must not be called the complete backlog. Detailed adopter qualification evidence stays private.

items.title: Whole-project private history transfer needs incremental ranges at long-term scale
items.cost: 0.5 exports/verifies a bounded whole-project archive (64 MiB default, up to 512 MiB, 2000 records/category). A long-lived busy store will exceed that cap; incremental/sharded exact-bound transfer with preserved references and resumable completeness is issue #67. Current behavior is an explicit cap failure, never silent pruning or a partial backup presented as full.

items.title: GitLab work scopes cannot certify exact-head approvals from the aggregate approvals API
items.cost: The 0.3.0 companion reads approval capability but the standard GitLab response supplies users/times, not the reviewed commit. It therefore keeps exact-head approval UNKNOWN and cannot admit automatic merges. A revision-bound read-only profile and adopter integration validation are tracked in https://github.com/drevendev/Devostasis/issues/58; this debt does not block independent review, issue, research or analysis work.

items.title: Conformance cases named in the specification have no executable fixture
items.cost: Closed as an implementation-fixture obligation in pending 0.6: the versioned bridge executes 63 permanent cases, materializing the former 62-case gap plus RPT-8. R11-R53 add 43 cases and 84 CI variants with native normalization and real governed/store/bundle lifecycles. B1 remains open for independent concrete-surface/whole-case exact-fixture acceptance and separate T9 cell-key delivery; capability or research expansion acceptance does not accept these local fixtures. No independent review is claimed.

items.title: The GitHub adapter makes unconditional requests and never backs off
items.cost: Every fleet run spent full API quota on evidence that mostly had not changed, and a rate-limited day degraded bands to UNKNOWN instead of reusing the previous answer. Closed in 0.1.6 by target B4: conditional requests replay unchanged bodies without spending quota, retryable failures wait only as long as the provider asked and only within a bounded waiting budget, and a per-project request budget truncates honestly instead of silently.

items.title: History is keyed by a mutable owner and name path
items.cost: Renaming or transferring a repository split its history in two: the old directory became an orphan and the new one started at BASELINE. Closed in 0.1.5 by target B2: the store locates a project by immutable_project_id, relocates the directory once and records the rename, and refuses to merge two projects into one directory.

items.title: Specification and provenance drift is caught only by a manual pass
items.cost: The research process found docs/spec/PROVENANCE.md describing a bundle lineage the code had already moved past, and the CHANGELOG calling a released version unreleased. Since 0.1.7 tests/test_spec_drift.py catches the mechanical half: a conformance citation that no longer resolves, a specification page missing from the index, and a contract identifier the runtime writes but the specification never names. The semantic half is still manual, because no test can tell whether a paragraph still describes what the code does.

items.title: The reusable workflow's default install ref is bumped by hand at every release
items.cost: observe-self.yml carries a default devostasis-ref, and the README and deployment guide carry the tag an adopter is told to pin. A release that forgets one installs an older engine for every caller that passes no ref. Since 0.1.3 tests/test_release_pins.py turns forgetting into a red build, and since 0.1.8 the Released pins resolve workflow turns a pin naming an unpublished tag into one too, after 0.1.8 shipped every pin pointing at a tag that did not exist. Both halves of the interest are now paid, but the bump is still manual and the obligation stays open until the version is generated rather than written.
